Article Title: Gold price crash: From Rs 1.80 lakh to below Rs 1.25 lakh, will gold now plunge to Rs 1 lakh per 10 gms?
Article Text:
Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached

Why has gold been crashing in 2026?

So, is there an end in sight to this fall? What should investors do, and does the crash mean that gold has lost its safe haven appeal. We ask experts:

Will gold fall to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams?

What Jateen Trivedi said

Has gold lost its safe haven status?

What Manav Modi said

What should investors do and what’s the outlook for 2027?

What Maneesh Sharma said

Gold is no longer glittery or shining - in fact gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In 2025, there seemed no end in sight for gold’s spectacular rally. Come 2026, the year started with the yellow metal hitting a lifetime high of Rs 1.8 lakh per 10 grams in futures contract.And then the story went downhill - with no immediate bottom in sight!In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce, its lowest level in over a year. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. The crash has been relatively less in India because the government hiked customs duty on gold and silver earlier this year, cushioning the fall to some extent.Gold started falling in January as investors booked profit, but before it could find its equilibrium, the US-Iran war triggered another crash.Analysts say that the recent decline reflects a combination of profit-booking, liquidation of leveraged positions, changing interest-rate expectations and a stronger dollar.Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks, where investors sold liquid gold positions to raise cash or meet margin calls rather than using it as a shield while elevated bond yields and expectations of tighter interest rates in the US raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached. So, does that mean that there is a chance of gold prices falling to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams as well?Experts don’t rule out the possibility, though they believe that underlying fundamentals of gold such as central bank buying will continue to support the yellow metal. This indicates that a further fall may not sustain for long, they say.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says, “A decline towards Rs 1,00,000 cannot be ruled out if the rupee appreciates significantly and COMEX Gold corrects towards $3,000.”“However, the more important question is whether such lower levels can sustain and establish a long-term base. Given rapidly changing global investment themes and persistent geopolitical uncertainty, I do not expect prices to sustain below Rs 1,15,000 for long,” Trivedi tells TOI.Manav Modi, Commodities Analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd says, “The breach of Rs 1.25 lakh highlights how quickly sentiment and price expectations can change in a highly volatile market.”But, the analyst notes that a fall towards Rs 1 lakh would require a deeper strength in story as well positioning, potentially driven by sustained dollar strength, higher real yields, continued speculative unwinding and a moderation in investment demand.“However, the extent of the recent correction also needs to be assessed against gold’s underlying physical and central bank demand, which remains an important structural support,” he tells TOI.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma says that technically, the spot gold pair has extended a bearish phase following the recent breakdown below the previous consolidation phase.Moreover, the yellow metal holds well below the technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) validating the negative outlook.“While oversold technical indicators like RSI indicate that downside pace could slow but not yet reverse the trend. Having said that, a near term consolidation is still possible but could not stop the extension of a recent well established downtrend making gold vulnerable to fall further up to $3420-3380 / Oz in Spot (CMP $ 3575/Oz). On MCX futures, a sustainable close below Rs. 1,21,000/10 gm could accelerate its downtrend towards Rs. 1,18,000-1,16,000/10 gm on MCX,” he tells TOI.No.Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities believes that even though gold has witnessed a sharp correction, this does not mean it has lost its safe-haven status.“If we look at the two-year performance, prices have risen from around Rs 75,000 in January 2025 to nearly Rs 1,25,000 currently, delivering returns of approximately 55%,” Trivedi points out.“An asset that has preserved value for over 5,000 years will inevitably experience cycles of profit booking and corrections. Gold's safe-haven appeal remains intact; recent weakness reflects changing market dynamics rather than a loss of its investment relevance,” he adds.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma is of the view that gold’s long term role as a monetary and currency hedge still remains intact as long-term drivers like central bank buying and sovereign debt concerns remain relevant over time.But, Manav Modi cautions that while gold may not have lost its appeal as a safe haven asset, the recent price movements highlight that it is not immune to sharp corrections, particularly when speculative positioning becomes stretched.“Safe haven demand can also take a backseat when investors prioritise liquidity and reduce exposure across asset classes. Gold’s underlying role as a portfolio diversifier and reserve asset remains intact,” he tells TOI.Gold continues to be supported by central bank buying and recently ETF inflows. According to the latest World Gold Council report, Central bank buying jumped to 321t in Q3, eclipsing recent typical quarterly buying levels and lifting ytd demand to 675t. Gold ETFs reversed course following the Q2 outflows, adding 211t in Q3.So if the yellow metal continues to be a safe haven asset, what should your investment strategy in the current situation be?Experts believe the ongoing correction can be a good opportunity to accumulate gold, though cautiously and keeping your overall portfolio balance in mind.“This correction offers an opportunity to review gold allocation rather than panic over falling prices or focus on previous highs near Rs 1,80,000,” Jateen Trivedi says.“Investors should evaluate their overall portfolio allocation and consider staggered accumulation. Those with less than 15% allocation to gold may consider adding gradually, including a small lump-sum investment if significantly underinvested. The focus should be on long-term portfolio diversification rather than timing the exact bottom,” he recommends.Manav Modi recommends a staggered strategy to accumulate gold. “But, since further downside cannot be ignored, post some clarity, accumulation could be looked at,” he says.Finally, where is gold headed in 2027?Maneesh Sharma shares that a 20-25% recovery to around $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support which translates to a level of Rs 1,45,000-1,50,000/10 gm on MCX futures contract.Jateen Trivedi too believes that gold could move towards Rs 1,55,000-Rs 1,65,000 over the next year, depending on international prices and the rupee's trajectory.“COMEX Gold could potentially revisit the $4,500 zone, supported by central-bank demand and geopolitical uncertainty. However, continued rupee appreciation could limit domestic gains, resulting in Indian gold underperforming international prices,” he says.
Article Summary: Gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks.

Article Title: Nvidia shares surge 35.5% as tech giant reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president
Article Text:
Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO (file photo)

What Jensen Huang said

Shares of Nvidia soared in trade on Monday after the tech giant announced the return of Jensen Huang as the company’s chief executive officer (CEO) with immediate effect. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave.The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. Earlier, the announcement triggered a sharp rally in the company's stock, which climbed more than 30% in premarket trading. The stock had recorded its steepest weekly fall since 2008 last week, after Huang’s removal from the CEO position unsettled investors and heightened worries about the future prospects of the AI sector.Jensen Huang’s unexpected return to the helm of Nvidia also triggered a broad rally in the US stock market. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week, one of its worst performances since the 2008 financial crisis.Technology stocks linked to artificial intelligence led the gains, pushing the Nasdaq Composite up 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1,117 points.Signs of a rebound had emerged even before Wall Street opened and Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement.Futures trading indicated that US stocks were poised to break a seven-session losing streak, with markets expected to open more than 2% higher.Meanwhile, European technology stocks also climbed 4.7% after Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.The decision represents a big departure of course for Nvidia's board, which had ruled out Huang's reinstatement only days earlier.Huang stepped down on November 12 following disclosures about extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for China. Beijing has denied the allegation.Explaining its decision to reinstate Huang, the board said it was satisfied with his candour and leadership capabilities. It added that, after consulting senior US government officials, it had concluded that his return posed no national security risk.“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” chair of the board Harvey C. Jones said in a statement Monday.Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.In a statement, Huang said he was “honored” to be back at the company and would take on the responsibility “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”He also expressed his gratitude to Jones, interim CEO Colette Kress, who will resume her position as CFO, and Nvidia’s executive staff for steering the company through the brief period of uncertainty.“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang’s statement continued. “Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family.I can’t wait to get back to work.”Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.
Article Summary: The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week.

Indians have always loved a good bargain, whether it is haggling over daily groceries or negotiating a trade deal with another country. After all, it is not a deal until you know you have secured better terms than the next person in line!After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact. However, the deal is yet to be signed.Earlier on Wednesday, India said it could sign the agreement only after the new tariff framework is in place and investigations under Section 301 are concluded.The India-US trade deal has seen several twists and turns since negotiations began in February 2025, from tariff threats and hopes of an agreement to a sudden courtroom setback. Now, with the deal back on the table, the latest development has raised a key question: What has changed, and why is the US suddenly offering the 'tariff king' a better deal?The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.Now, Washington's willingness to give India a comparative tariff advantage over its peers has brought the negotiations back into focus.India's importance to Washington goes well beyond trade figures. Its vast consumer market, supply of affordable medicines and potential to emerge as an alternative manufacturing base to China give the US several reasons to keep the partnership strong.Tariff competitiveness is another important part of the equation. When the first-phase BTA framework was finalised, India enjoyed a tariff advantage over ASEAN nations — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia — as well as Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh.But a lower tariff does not always mean a better deal.If India's rivals secure bigger tariff cuts, their products could become cheaper in the US market, leaving Indian exporters struggling to compete. The real advantage, therefore, lies not just in lower duties but in ensuring that India remains ahead of its competitors.So, what makes India a partner Washington cannot afford to overlook?India's importance to the US goes beyond trade, particularly when it comes to medicines. The country supplies 47% of US generic prescription drugs and 60% of hypertension medicines. Steep tariffs could hit American consumers and patients first.Rohit Kumar Singh of Eminence Strategy Consulting warns, “Disruption in supply might impact American citizens directly.”Replacing approved manufacturers, he adds, takes both investment and time.Even when the US threatened a 100% tariff on pharmaceutical imports, India remained largely shielded. Generics account for over 90% of medicines used in America and were exempted to avoid shortages and price spikes.Similarly, under the February 6 framework, the US had proposed scrapping reciprocal tariffs on Indian generics and their ingredients, with further concessions subject to a separate US investigation.The proposed purchases under the interim trade framework also give American businesses a reason to support closer trade ties with India.Under an earlier statement, India had indicated its intention to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years. These included energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal.For perspective, India's imports from all countries stood at $527.21 billion during April-October 2026-27.Singh adds that pushing India too hard could jeopardise these potential sales.As Sandeep Gupta of Executive Access sums it up, “It’s a ‘we can scratch each other’s back effectively’ deal that works for both sides.”With over 140 crore people, India is a shopper's paradise for American brands. Nearly 65% of Indians are under 35, and rising household incomes are expected to drive demand across categories, from appliances and cars to IT services. This creates opportunities for American companies selling technology, parts and financing.Geopolitics expert Jagvinder Singh Virk told TOI, “This young demographic, our expanding middle class, growing purchasing power and rapidly developing economy make India one of the most attractive markets in the world.”The US already sold India $45.4 billion worth of goods and $42.9 billion worth of services in 2025, according to USTR. Walking away from the partnership could mean losing access to an expanding market and future customers.Global companies do not just want to sell in India; they also want to manufacture here and benefit from its growth.Virk says, “India is also emerging as a trusted global manufacturing and supply-chain partner.”Despite a bumpy global economic environment, India's exports grew over 16% in the first seven months of FY 2026-27.The US increasingly sees India as a strategic economic partner rather than just another trading destination. Its willingness to offer the country a tariff advantage over competing economies also reflects India's growing bargaining power in trade negotiations.India-US relations extend beyond trade, with both countries sharing strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.One example is the Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, which focuses on cooperation in maritime security and critical technologies. In May 2026, the four countries launched an Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance project and a framework to strengthen critical-mineral supply chains.Singh cautions that any weakening of this partnership “will make it harder to implement plans to develop alternatives to concentrated supply networks.”Ritik Bhandari, team lead, Centre for Law, Policy and Governance, NFPRC Foundation says that India's growing importance to the US is driven by both economic opportunities and shared strategic interests.He further points out that India offers Washington a large consumer base, manufacturing capabilities and scope for collaboration in technology and energy. Its role in diversifying global supply chains and strengthening the US presence in the Indo-Pacific further adds to its importance.The proposed tariff advantage, he says, reflects Washington's intention to ensure India remains competitive against other trading partners.For years, China has been America's factory floor, supplying everything from electronics to industrial components. But Washington is now looking to reduce that dependence, and India is emerging as an important alternative.Gupta said, “The US wants to reduce its dependence on China-dominated manufacturing items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, minerals and manufacturing, which India can effectively offer.”US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer echoed this view in an interview with Fox News, acknowledging that “India can be a way station for that.”Losing India's trust, therefore, could prove costly for Washington on two fronts. American exporters risk losing access to Indian consumers, while US manufacturers could find themselves with fewer alternatives to Chinese suppliers.India has made it clear that a trade deal cannot come at any cost. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had earlier said negotiations had reached a stage where further give-and-take would be “very, very difficult”, describing the pact as a “hard and very vigorously negotiated agreement”.Both countries, however, maintain that they are working towards a fair and mutually beneficial deal. US embassy deputy chief of mission Jason Meeks recently described the proposed partnership as “fair, reciprocal, and mutually beneficial”, with cooperation extending beyond goods.According to Jagvinder Singh Virk, India changed the tone of negotiations with “a clear economic vision, well-defined priorities and a willingness to find practical solutions”. New Delhi, he said, had shown that it could protect its core interests while remaining flexible where both sides stood to gain.Washington, too, has reasons not to push too hard. India offers US companies a vast consumer market, a young workforce, growing manufacturing capabilities and an opportunity to diversify supply chains.Comparing the talks with negotiations involving Canada and South Korea, Virk said India's growing economic strength and strategic importance set it apart.India, meanwhile, remains firm on sensitive sectors such as agriculture and dairy. It is open to a deal, but wants one that safeguards its interests and recognises its growing economic role.India-US ties may finally be turning a corner.Chief economic adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said recent weeks had shown signs of easing tensions, adding that a trade deal in early December could mean “we may have seen the worst of the unsettled phase behind us”.One of the bigger questions is whether the agreement can help India reduce its dependence on China. Initiatives such as Make in India, the PLI scheme and Aatmanirbhar Bharat offer a starting point. However, India must build its own manufacturing capabilities rather than simply replace dependence on China with dependence on the US.The next step, therefore, is to strengthen domestic capacity. Bhandari added that manufacturing incentives could encourage Indian companies to produce more raw materials at home, while long-term US orders could help fund these facilities."The government's focus on domestic manufacturing, infrastructure development and initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides a strong foundation for this transition. Importantly, India is approaching this partnership from a position of strategic autonomy, seeking to expand international economic cooperation while strengthening its domestic capabilities.This is an opportunity to reinforce India's economic resilience and global standing," Bhandari said.At the same time, India needs to find alternative sources for critical inputs. The real opportunity is not just to become an alternative to China, but to emerge as a manufacturing and technology powerhouse in its own right.
Article Summary: After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies. The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. But the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.

Article Title: Elderly man sells property to son-in-law and faces Rs 20.94 lakh tax penalty for alleged cash transaction; ITAT finds no proof of cash receipt and cancels penalty, also deletes additions over farm inc
Article Text:
The ITAT deleted the Rs 20.94 lakh penalty because the taxpayer consistently denied receiving the cash. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT Hyderabad rule in favour of property seller?

An elderly taxpayer faced a penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh after the Income Tax Department concluded that he had received this amount in cash while selling a property to his son-in-law, in contravention of the Income Tax Act.The Income Tax Department did not accept his explanation at the first appellate stage and sustained the penalty. Read on to know why the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) gave relief.The dispute centred on the sale of an immovable property. The AO concluded that the taxpayer had received Rs 20.94 lakh in cash in connection with the transfer, thereby breaching Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act.A penalty equivalent to the disputed amount was then imposed under Section 271D. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), also subsequently upheld the penalty.The property seller then challenged the department's finding that any cash had changed hands.The taxpayer explained that, being elderly, he had decided to sell his property to his son-in-law for an agreed consideration of Rs 45.50 lakh. The sale deed was executed on August 12, 2015, when the property's stamp duty value stood at Rs 66.44 lakh.The taxpayer contended that the advocate drafting the sale deed had entered the difference of Rs 20.94 lakh as cash received solely to make the consideration recorded in the document correspond with the property's stamp duty value. He maintained throughout that he had not actually received this sum in cash.Challenging the penalty before the ITAT, the taxpayer argued that the department had incorrectly treated the amount recorded in the sale deed as proof of an actual cash receipt.The tax department also raised questions about certain deposits, which the taxpayer attributed to his agricultural activities and a loan.On October 9, 2026, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Hyderabad, ruled in the elderly man’s favour, cancelling the penalty and granting relief in respect of these additions.The ITAT deleted the Rs 20.94 lakh penalty because the taxpayer consistently denied receiving the cash, and his son-in-law supported this claim through an affidavit stating that no cash had been paid.Although the sale deed recorded the amount as received, the Assessing Officer had not examined the son-in-law to verify the alleged payment. The tribunal considered these facts along with the explanation that the amount had been included to match the stamp duty value and the family circumstances surrounding the property transfer.It concluded that the taxpayer had established reasonable cause under Section 273B of the Income Tax Act, which provides relief from penalties in such circumstances, and directed the penalty to be deleted.“The man pointed out that the Assessing Officer had not examined the son-inlaw or independently verified whether the payment had actually taken place,” Advocate K Sai Teja, practising in the Supreme Court of India told ET.In view of these circumstances, the Tribunal found reasonable cause for the alleged breach under Section 273B and ordered the Income Tax Department to remove the entire penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh, he adds.The tribunal's decision did not amount to a conclusive finding that no cash had changed hands simply because the taxpayer denied receiving the money. It recognised that the statement recorded in a registered sale deed constituted relevant evidence and could not be rejected merely on the basis of a later denial.ITAT also removed tax additions linked to agricultural income and a loanIn a separate appeal relating to the same assessment year, the taxpayer contested additions made by the Income Tax Department during reassessment proceedings. The AO had identified cash deposits of Rs 48.60 lakh in the taxpayer's bank account, along with time deposits totalling Rs 13 lakh. Since the taxpayer had not filed an income tax return for assessment year 2016-17, the AO completed the reassessment on March 21, 2024, assessing his total income at Rs 87.48 lakh.Among the adjustments made, the AO classified certain amounts claimed to be agricultural income and a loan as unexplained money under Section 69A of the Income Tax Act.The taxpayer maintained that he owned 4.86 acres of agricultural land, which he had leased to two individuals for cultivation. The land was used to grow sunflower seeds, and the cultivators transferred his one-third share of the proceeds from the sale of the produce through banking channels. The two receipts under dispute amounted to Rs 1.38 lakh and Rs 1.20 lakh.Arguing against the additions, the taxpayer said the money represented his share of the agricultural produce and, therefore, could not be classified as unexplained. The ITAT observed that the ownership of the agricultural land, the cultivation activities and the receipt of the disputed amounts through banking channels were not in question.Since the tax department had not furnished evidence to disprove the taxpayer's explanation, the tribunal directed the AO to remove both additions. The amounts deleted were Rs 1,38,000 and Rs 1,20,250, respectively.The tribunal also granted relief on another addition of Rs 3 lakh, which the taxpayer said he had borrowed from an individual. In support of his explanation, he furnished a bank statement and a confirmation from the lender.
Article Summary: An elderly taxpayer faced a penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh after the Income Tax Department concluded that he had received this amount in cash while selling a property. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Hyderabad, ruled in the elderly man’s favour, cancelling the penalty and granting relief in respect of these additions.

Article Title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down after 11 years
Article Text:
Kalyan Krishnamurthy

NEW DELHI: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group on Wednesday announced that CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down from his role and leave the company after more than 11 years, Reuters reported.Krishnamurthy has led the e-commerce giant through its acquisition by Walmart and years of preparations for a long-awaited initial public offering (IPO).The company is expected to announce Krishnamurthy's successor in the coming weeks. Balaji Thiagarajan, currently Flipkart 's chief product and technology officer will lead the organisation in the interim, the company said.Flipkart, one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, has more than 500 million registered users. Walmart said it "remains committed" to Flipkart and its long-term opportunity in India.Krishnamurthy joined Flipkart in 2016 and was appointed CEO in January 2017. During his tenure, he led several key businesses, including category operations, marketing, customer shopping experience, marketplace, retail advertising and private labels.Krishnamurthy had also served as the company's interim CFO in 2013 during an earlier association.Before joining Flipkart, Krishnamurthy served as managing director at Tiger Global Management, where he managed the fund's India portfolio companies.He was also director of finance for portfolio companies at the investment firm.He previously worked at eBay Asia Pacific as director of financial planning and analysis and served as country finance director for eBay South Asia in Hong Kong. Earlier in his career, he worked with Procter & Gamble in its supply chain finance business.Krishnamurthy holds an MBA from the Asian Institute of Management in the Philippines.

Incentives will then be disbursed over the following five years, based on incremental sales of eligible equipment and components. The final year will be used to settle incentives for the last year of the disbursement period.The scheme is aimed at technologically advanced construction and infrastructure equipment used across major infrastructure and industrial projects.The government has specifically identified:The scheme also covers eligible components manufactured by approved applicants, rather than focusing only on finished equipment.The government expects the incentives to expand domestic manufacturing capacity, improve the availability of equipment and components, strengthen supply chains and create employment opportunities.The proposed testing facility is another part of the effort to develop the domestic manufacturing ecosystem.With the CIE market projected to grow from around Rs 97,500 crore in 2024-25 to Rs 2.28 lakh crore by 2029-30, the scheme is intended to support manufacturers as demand for construction and infrastructure equipment rises.The government has positioned the initiative as part of its Atmanirbhar Bharat agenda, with the stated objective of making India more self-reliant in technologically advanced equipment manufacturing and more competitive in global markets.

Article Title: The onion index: How rising pyaaz prices can make your EMIs and investment portfolio cry
Article Text:
Onion prices have been rising steadily this year, and for the last two months have been the item with the highest inflation.

So why are onion prices so closely tracked? What does a rise in onion price mean for you beyond the obvious rise in your grocery and food budget?

Why have onion prices been rising and what do they mean for inflation?

Retail Onion Prices

How it impacts RBI’s decision making

How it impacts your EMIs

How a repo rate hike hits your home loan

How it impacts Sensex and companies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Onions are a staple food in Indian households, but their ability to make you cry can stretch beyond your kitchens! In fact, until some years ago any major rise in onion prices used to be an important election issue.Onion prices have been rising steadily this year, and for the last two months have been the item with the highest inflation. According to government data, retail prices of 41 out of 42 essential commodities have risen over the year. But onions stand out with their over 100% inflation rate.Onion prices have risen due to supply side issues. Depletion and some spoilage of stored rabi stocks and concerns over the timing and quality of kharif arrivals amid uneven rainfall have led to the sudden spike.In September this year, TOI reported that at Lasalgaon APMC in Nashik, wholesale onion prices climbed 160% in less than three months, from Rs 1,740 per quintal on June 22 to Rs 4,550 on September 5, 2026!Delayed monsoon rainfall has disrupted kharif onion planting across Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.Trade sources attributed the onion price surge to an estimated 5-7% decline in Maharashtra’s kharif onion production, linked to reduced acreage and delayed monsoon rains.Not just that, the unseasonal rain during the summer harvest reduced the shelf life of stored onions and accelerated their spoilage.A recent Reserve Bank of India (RBI) report acknowledges that the rise in onion prices this year has been higher than that seen in recent years. Onion prices have increased by about 84% since end-June (up to September 30).“Although onion prices exhibit a seasonal uptick during August-September before the arrival of the kharif crops, the magnitude of increase has been much higher this year than the historical average,” it notes.The Onion Price Index - both wholesale and retail - has crossed 100% in September and October this year!Onion prices form an important part of food inflation. The CPI Onion Index has a weightage of 24.36% in food inflation, and 0.70% in overall inflation. The CPI Food Index in turn has a weightage of 34.78% in overall inflation, making food prices an important part of the inflation data and its fluctuations.RBI is mandated to maintain retail inflation in the 2-6% range, with 4% serving to be the ideal target. However, in October this year, CPI inflation crossed the 6% threshold for the first time in several months.In anticipation of the approaching inflation hike, the central bank-led Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has already hiked the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. With the inflation number now crossing 6%, economists see a December rate hike as a foregone conclusion.While some economists see the possibility of a 50 basis points hike, others say the RBI may take a more cautious approach, awaiting to see the impact of falling global crude oil prices and the seasonal food price spike settling.A disproportionate rise in onion prices, hence feeds into inflation and in turn can impact the RBI’s repo rate math.However, Ranen Banerjee, Partner and Leader, Economic Advisory, PwC India notes that a rise in onion prices alone is not enough to sway RBI’s decisions, especially as many factors governing onion prices are beyond its control.“The MPC does not look at a particular commodity’s price in making its rate setting decision. The price of onions are highly sensitive to supply side factors that a monetary policy cannot effectively address. The current high prices are owing to lesser supplies in the mandis from the farms and these generally get addressed with new arrivals or government interventions on the supply side,” Banerjee tells TOI.When inflation rises sharply, the RBI must assess whether it is a temporary supply shock or whether higher prices could spread across the economy.RBI’s October rate hike cited wider inflation concerns, including food and fuel pressures. It’s important to note that while the decision was not attributable to onions alone, food prices continue to play an important role.So, even though a single commodity or food price may not influence RBI decisions, it definitely feeds into the overall inflation number, which the RBI tries to keep in check through repo rate decisions.If you are wondering what onion prices have to do with your monthly EMI payouts - the link runs through monetary policy.Repo rate is the interest rate at which banks are able to borrow money from the central bank. A hike in that makes borrowing costlier for banks, and they in turn make their loans costlier by hiking their lending rates.Every time the RBI hikes the repo rate, you may feel a pinch in terms of higher EMIs, unless you are on a fixed interest loan. This means that you either have to pay higher EMIs if you want to pay your loan within the stipulated time, or you have to increase your loan tenure in a bid to keep your EMI constant. In both scenarios your total outgo on the loan goes up as the interest component of your loan rises.So a rise in food or onion prices not just impacts your household kitchen budget, it also has the ability to shrink your spending capability by raising your debt repayment outgo.A rise in interest rates also tends to feed negatively into the stock market, as other interest yielding asset classes become more attractive.But, experts say that the stock market has already priced in the possibility of another repo rate hike. In fact, Sensex has been on a record winning spree since late October as sentiment has turned favourable.“After the 25 basis points increase in the repo rate to 5.50% in October and the shift in policy stance to calibrated tightening, we expect a further 25 bps hike in December, taking the repo rate to 5.75%, followed by another 50bp over subsequent meetings,” ⁠Sneha Poddar, VP-Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services tells TOI.“A gradual pace of tightening is largely priced in, though a sharper-than-expected increase could weigh on market sentiment in the near term; a significant correction, however, appears unlikely,” she says.For companies selling packaged foods, household products and other everyday goods, higher food inflation can squeeze consumers' disposable incomes. Households may cut back on discretionary purchases to accommodate higher grocery bills. Companies exposed to food ingredients may also face higher costs, which can hurt profit margins if they cannot pass them on to customers.According to Sneha Poddar, banks, including public sector banks, are positioned to benefit.“In a rising rate environment, lending rates reset almost immediately while deposit costs adjust with a lag, supporting profitability. Non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), which rely on borrowed funds, may face pressure on margins,” she explains.“Real estate, automobiles and discretionary consumption are the most exposed, facing valuation and demand headwinds. Capital-intensive infrastructure, utilities and leveraged firms face higher financing costs, and a prolonged tightening cycle could delay private investment. We see crude oil, food inflation and the rupee as the key variables to monitor,” she adds.
Article Summary: Onion prices have been rising steadily this year, and for the last two months have been the item with the highest inflation. Retail prices of 41 out of 42 essential commodities have risen over the year, but onions stand out with their over 100% inflation rate. The Onion Price Index - both wholesale and retail - has crossed 100% in September and October this year!

Article Title: From construction equipment to postal services: Cabinet clears Rs 19,934 crore package; key decisions
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw speaks during a Union Cabinet briefing in New Delhi

Rs 11,000 crore scheme to boost construction equipment manufacturing

New container terminal at Kamarajar Port

Greenfield airport approved for Doloo in Assam

Postal Operations Scheme gets Rs 1,141 crore

Rs 1,491 crore for modernising postal infrastructure

Increased employment opportunities Boost to export-import activities Improved infrastructure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a series of proposals involving a combined outlay of nearly Rs 19,934 crore, including an Rs 11,000-crore scheme to strengthen India's construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing ecosystem, a new container terminal in Tamil Nadu and a greenfield airport in Assam.The decisions were announced by Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at a press briefing following the Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The Cabinet also approved the continuation of two schemes for the Department of Posts during the 16th Finance Commission period, from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with a combined outlay of Rs 2,632 crore.Here are the key decisions announced at the briefing:The Cabinet approved the Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem with a financial outlay of Rs 11,000 crore.The scheme, to be implemented by the ministry of heavy industries over eight years from 2026-27, aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment and components. It also provides for setting up a dedicated testing facility in the country.According to the government, India's construction and infrastructure equipment industry was the world's third largest, after China and the US, with a market size of around Rs 97,500 crore in 2024-25.It is projected to more than double to around Rs 2.28 lakh crore by 2029-30.The scheme will have two components: sales-linked incentives for eligible original equipment manufacturers and component makers, with rates ranging from 13% to 8% of incremental sales over five years; and a grant of up to Rs 375 crore for setting up a dedicated testing facility.The government said the initiative would support domestic production of equipment such as ship-to-shore cranes, tunnel boring machines, hydraulic excavators and off-highway trucks.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu at an estimated project cost of Rs 4,288.26 crore, including GST.The project will be developed under the public-private partnership model on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer basis. It will involve construction of a 900-metre-long terminal with an annual handling capacity of two million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).The project will be implemented in two phases. The first phase will have a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, while the second will add 0.9 million TEUs. The terminal will have a design draft of 18 metres and will be capable of handling large container vessels, including ships with a capacity of up to 24,346 TEUs.The concessionaire will arrange the investment for the terminal, while Kamarajar Port Limited will separately bear an estimated Rs 450 crore towards dredging. The concession period will be 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months.The government said the additional capacity would help meet rising containerised export-import demand from the Chennai-Ennore industrial region and the wider southern hinterland. The project is expected to generate around 750 direct and indirect jobs during construction and increase employment by about 800 people during operations.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs also approved a greenfield airport at Doloo in Assam's Cachar district, near Silchar, at an estimated cost of Rs 2,014 crore.The Airports Authority of India will develop the airport to address the operational and space constraints of the existing civil enclave at Silchar Airport, which is located on defence land, and accommodate rising passenger traffic.The proposed terminal will cover 12,351 square metres and will be able to handle 800 passengers during peak hours. The project also includes a 2,705-metre-long runway, designed for A-320 aircraft operations, and an apron with parking capacity for six A-320 aircraft, along with a dedicated isolation bay.The government said the airport would improve air connectivity for South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring states, while supporting trade, tourism and economic activity in the Barak Valley.The Cabinet approved the continuation of the Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs 1,141 crore for the five-year period from 2026-27 to 2030-31.The scheme aims to modernise India Post's network, improve mail and parcel operations, strengthen last-mile delivery and expand citizen-centric services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.It includes six components covering rural access to the postal network, mail and parcel network optimisation, international mail infrastructure, marketing and service quality, and philately operations.The largest allocation of Rs 575 crore is for mail network optimisation, including modernisation of mail handling, delivery systems and transport networks. Parcel network optimisation has been allocated Rs 278 crore, while Rs 120 crore will go towards improving rural access and postal infrastructure.Other allocations include Rs 100 crore for marketing and service quality, Rs 60 crore for philately operations and Rs 8 crore for international mail infrastructure.India Post operates a network of 1.65 lakh post offices, including nearly 1.5 lakh in rural areas. The government said the scheme would support its expanding role in parcel delivery, e-commerce logistics, financial inclusion and digital services.The Cabinet also approved the continuation of the Estates Management Scheme for the Department of Posts, with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore over five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31.The scheme aims to modernise post office buildings and residential colonies through new construction, reconstruction, renovation and uniform branding. It also includes the restoration of heritage postal buildings.Under the plan, Rs 280 crore has been earmarked to construct 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant land, while Rs 108 crore will be used to rebuild 50 dilapidated structures. Another Rs 318 crore will go towards renovating and branding 2,550 departmental sub-post offices.The scheme also provides Rs 37.5 crore to upgrade 2,500 post offices operating from rented premises and Rs 180 crore to restore 20 heritage postal buildings. A further Rs 357.5 crore has been allocated for renovating 150 postal residential colonies.The remaining provisions include Rs 100 crore for sustainable and accessibility-related facilities, such as solar power, rainwater harvesting, ramps and Braille signage, and Rs 100 crore for an integrated technology centre in Bengaluru to support postal technology services.
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a series of proposals involving a combined outlay of nearly Rs 19,934 crore. The proposals include a Rs 11,000-crore scheme to strengthen India's construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing ecosystem. A new container terminal in Tamil Nadu and a greenfield airport in Assam were also approved.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari launched India’s first barrier-free tolling in May 2026; now NHAI’s net revenue from the system has risen by 19.84% to Rs 539 crore across seven plazas in just six months
Article Text:
According to the government, the shift to barrier-free toll collection has delivered considerable operational and financial benefits. (Image for representative purpose only)

Barrier-free tolling launched this year

Understanding barrier-free tolling

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In what is being seen as a major boost from barrier-free tolling use, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has recorded a 19.84% rise in net toll collections to Rs 538.95 crore between May and October 2026 through the system.The barrier-free Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system is functional across seven operational fee plazas.The government is introducing Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) technology across national highways as part of its move towards barrier-free toll collection.The system is being viewed as the next stage in the evolution of FASTag . Although FASTag has enabled digital toll payments, motorists still have to reduce their speed and pass through designated toll lanes and physical barriers.On May 1, 2026, Road Transport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari launched the country’s first barrier-free tolling system at the Choryasi Fee Plaza in Gujarat.It was subsequently rolled out at Mundka, Daulatpura, Gharaunda, Manoharpura, Shahjahanpur and Paranur. The Nemili and Chenasamudram fee plazas began operating under the system in November 2026.Excluding Nemili and Chenasamudram, the operational plazas collectively generated net toll revenue of Rs 538.95 crore, compared with Rs 449.72 crore during the corresponding pre-MLFF period in 2025."As on October 31, 2026, the cumulative performance across these seven plazas indicates an increase of 19.84 per cent in net revenue to NHAI, compared to the corresponding pre-MLFF baseline. Transaction volumes have also registered significant growth," NHAI said in a statement.The state-owned authority said the shift to barrier-free toll collection has delivered considerable operational and financial benefits. However, it has also encountered cases in which vehicle owners deliberately obscure, cover or tamper with their registration number plates to avoid paying tolls."NHAI has taken serious cognizance of such instances and is closely coordinating with the concerned state governments and enforcement agencies to ensure strict action against such defaulters," NHAI said.The statement said police check posts have been set up at select MLFF locations, including Gharaunda Fee Plaza. Vehicles caught engaging in such practices are being stopped and issued challans under the applicable provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.NHAI is also introducing technology-based measures powered by artificial intelligence to identify these vehicles and trace their registered owners. These include Vehicle Fingerprinting and integration with the VAHAN database, the authority said.It added that electronic notices are being issued to recover unpaid user fees. Where the dues remain unpaid despite these notices, access to applicable VAHAN services is being restricted in line with the prescribed enforcement framework.Under barrier-free tolling, vehicles are able to continue travelling at normal highway speeds as cameras and FASTag technology identify them and deduct the applicable toll automatically.FASTag has become central to India's electronic toll collection system. FASTag is also serving as the payment mechanism for India's transition to barrier-free tolling.The technology combines Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), AI-based analytics and FASTag-enabled electronic toll collection to replace the physical barriers that currently require vehicles to slow down at toll plazas.With this arrangement, tolls can be collected without motorists having to stop, reduce speed or remain in a designated lane. Once a vehicle crosses a specified point, the system identifies it, automatically deducts the toll from its FASTag account and sends a notification to the user.
Article Summary: National Highways Authority of India recorded a 19.84% rise in net toll collections to Rs 538.95 crore between May and October 2026 through the system. The barrier-free Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system is functional across seven operational fee plazas.

Article Title: Egg prices fall as much as 20% in just 8-10 days as bird flu stalls exports from Tamil Nadu, which accounts for over 90% of India’s egg exports; but farmers face 30%-50% higher feed costs
Article Text:
The price squeeze is also hurting poultry farmers producing chicken. (Image for representative purpose only)

Egg prices crash and demand falls

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports. Egg prices have crashed anywhere between 10%-20% over the past 8-10 days.The surplus supplies are being directed into the domestic market at a time when seasonal demand is already losing momentum in southern India.Farm-gate prices, which had climbed following Chhath Puja, have now begun falling, upsetting poultry farmers who had anticipated better returns during the winter months.Consumption demand in southern states has also weakened during the Hindu month of Karthik, adding to the excess supply in the market.The price drop has come even as production expenses remain high, according to an ET report. Maize and soybean, two key ingredients used in poultry feed, have become 30%-50% more expensive than a year ago, putting further pressure on farmers’ margins.Poultry feed primarily comprises ingredients such as maize, broken rice, soybean meal and millets. Maize prices have risen by around 50% over the past year, while soybean meal has become approximately 30% more expensive.Soybean meal is a by-product obtained when soybean seeds are crushed to extract oil. Poultry industry players and farmers had been counting on higher realisations during winter, when egg and chicken consumption typically increases across India.Egg prices had begun moving upwards across the country after Chhath Puja, reaching a peak of Rs 6.70 per egg in Namakkal, India’s poultry hub, on November 11. However, the upward trend quickly reversed after bird flu was confirmed in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, on November 13. The outbreak prompted containment measures, including the culling of birds and a 90-day prohibition on raising poultry in the affected area.In Namakkal, egg prices fell to Rs 5.60 apiece, marking a decline of around 19%. The fall has been relatively modest in Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat and Maharashtra, where prices have dropped by about 6%-10%, while most southern states have recorded declines exceeding 15%.“Namakkal in Tamil Nadu is India’s egg export hub and accounts for over 90% of the country’s egg exports. The region was exporting about one crore eggs per day last year during the same time, which had reduced to about 15-20 eggs per day just before the outbreak,” Sanjeev Chintawar, chief operating officer, National Egg Coordination Committee told the financial daily.The seasonal dip in demand has compounded the oversupply in southern India, as consumption of non-vegetarian food is restricted during Karthik, a month in the Indian calendar. “Farmers had reduced production for two months before Diwali to cope with the higher feed costs and planned to increase production in winter hoping to get better realisation,” said Chintawar.He added, “With feed suppliers refusing to sell feed on credit to the poultry farmers due to supressed prices of eggs and chicken, bird nutrition has been adversely affected either knowingly or unknowingly.”The price squeeze is also hurting poultry farmers producing chicken. “Farmers are bleeding. The production cost of chicken is over 120/kg, while farmers are getting just about 80/kg,” said KG Anand, general manager, Venkateshwara Hatcheries, the largest fully integrated poultry conglomerate of India.The wider feed industry is also struggling amid the downturn. “Everyone is making losses. We have no clue how to survive this situation,” said Divya Kumar Gulati, immediate past president, Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association of India, the industry body representing the animal feed industry.
Article Summary: Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports. The surplus supplies are being directed into the domestic market at a time when seasonal demand is already losing momentum in southern India. Maize and soybean, two key ingredients used in poultry feed, have become 30%-50% more expensive than a year ago.

Article Title: Stock market today: Sensex ends over 1,500 point after 2,000 point surge, Nifty50 crosses 25,800 - Investors richer by Rs 3.84 lakh crore!
Article Text:
Stock market rallies.

Top 5 reasons behind the stock market rally

1. Strong foreign fund inflows

2. Lower crude oil prices

3. Rupee rises 23 paise against US dollar

4. Heavyweight banking stocks lead gains

5. Strong corporate earnings support sentiment

6. Markets rebound despite global AI-led volatility

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

NEW DELHI: Indian benchmark indices staged a sharp rebound on Wednesday, recovering from Monday's selloff as foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices and buying in heavyweight banking stocks lifted sentiment, despite weak global cues and concerns over AI-linked stocks.The BSE Sensex surged 1,502.29 points, or 1.82%, to close at 83,938.28, while the Nifty 50 gained 469.60 points, or 1.85%, to settle at 25,819.25.During the intra-day trading session, the Sensex climbed 2,062.22 points, or 2.50%, to hit an intraday high of 84,498.21, while the Nifty rallied 602 points, or 2.37%, to 25,951.65.The rally added Rs 3.84 lakh crore to investors' wealth, taking the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 513 lakh crore.The gains followed Monday's sharp decline, when the Sensex plunged 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%, to 82,435.99, while the Nifty fell 450.95 points, or 1.75%, to 25,349.65. Markets were closed on Tuesday for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.Strong foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil prices, buying in heavyweight banking stocks and resilient corporate earnings supported domestic equities. Investors also appeared to rotate out of crowded AI-linked trades amid continued volatility in global markets.From the Sensex pack, Hindustan Unilever was the top gainer, rising 5.94%, followed by Trent (3.59%), ICICI Bank (3.44%), InterGlobe Aviation (3.24%), HDFC Bank (3.18%) and Bajaj Finance (3.04%).Tata Steel, Bharti Airtel and Titan ended lower.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to buy Indian equities, providing strong support to domestic markets. Foreign investors purchased shares worth Rs 5,672.99 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.Foreign inflows into India have strengthened this month, reflecting a reversal in investor sentiment towards domestic equities.V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said, "The total reversal of the FII stance towards India is reflected in the FII investment into India, so far, this month at a record $13.2 billion."Crude oil prices eased on Wednesday, offering some relief to India's macroeconomic outlook by easing inflationary concerns and potentially lowering the country's import bill. Brent crude, the global benchmark, fell 0.19% to $91.38 per barrel.Brent crude futures had earlier declined 0.5% to $90.97 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 0.6% to $81.58. Both benchmarks had risen more than 2% on Tuesday.Oil prices remain under pressure amid rising supply and expectations of a market surplus, offsetting concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.Rupee strengthened 23 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, supported by foreign fund inflows, strong domestic equities and lower crude oil prices.The rupee opened at 92.65 in the interbank foreign exchange market and subsequently gained to 92.62 against the greenback.A stronger US dollar, however, capped gains in the domestic currency. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, rose 0.15% to 103.90.Earlier on Monday, rupee had declined 23 paise to close at 92.85 against the dollar, retreating from its seven-month high.Banking stocks were among the biggest contributors to the market rally, with strong buying in heavyweight private lenders lifting benchmark indices.HDFC Bank surged 3.54%, ICICI Bank rose 3.19%, Bajaj Finance advanced 2.65%, Axis Bank added 2.13% and Bajaj Finserv climbed 2.09%.The Nifty Private Bank index gained 2.27%, while the Nifty PSU Bank index rose 0.68%.Financial stocks gained 2.2% in broader sectoral trade, with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Reliance Industries also among the major contributors to the rally.Domestic earnings have provided support to Indian equities despite volatility in global markets.Vijayakumar said, "It is important to understand that India’s improving fundamentals, as reflected in the impressive 27% earnings growth of Nifty 50 in Q2 has the potential to support the increasing FII inflows and impart resilience to the market."Investors have also been shifting funds towards Indian equities as global markets face uncertainty over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector."Earnings have provided a domestic anchor, while rotation away from Asian AI trades have also helped redirect capital towards India," Venkatesh Balasubramaniam and Shanay Mehta of JM Financial told Reuters.A sharp correction in crude prices has also reduced pressure on the macroeconomic outlook, the analyst added.Indian equities staged a strong recovery despite weakness in global markets, where technology stocks remained under pressure amid concerns over high AI valuations and rising infrastructure spending.Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as investors booked profits in technology stocks and turned cautious ahead of key US inflation data. Nvidia fell nearly 6%, while Anthropic's shares slipped below their IPO price.The selloff reflected concerns over whether the massive investments in data centres, chips and other AI infrastructure would generate returns quickly enough to justify current valuations. The weakness also spread to technology-heavy Asian markets, including South Korea, Japan and Taiwan.However, India's IT sector has a different exposure to the AI ecosystem. Companies such as Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, HCLTech and Wipro primarily operate asset-light technology services businesses.V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said sharp movements in global markets were being driven largely by volatility in AI-linked stocks."There is heightened volatility in global equity markets caused mainly by the swings in AI trade. When the Nasdaq goes down other AI markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, too, go down; when Nasdaq bounces back, these AI trade-dominated markets, too, bounce back. The derivatives trade is aggravating the down moves and up moves in the market, as happened in India last Monday," he said.He advised investors to look beyond short-term market swings and focus on fundamentals."Investors should ignore these wild moves and noise associated with this hyper speculative trade and focus on the fundamentals. From the fundamentals perspective, the Indian market looks resilient," he added.The gains in India extended beyond frontline stocks, with the Nifty 100 rising 1.38%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.89% and 0.48%, respectively.Among sectoral indices, the Nifty IT jumped 2.39% and the Nifty Private Bank advanced 2.27%. The Nifty FMCG gained 0.96%, the Nifty Pharma rose 0.98% and the Nifty Auto edged up 0.19%.In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi tumbled 6.16 per cent, Japan's Nikkei 225 was down 2.78 per cent, Shanghai's SSE Composite index declined 2.03 per cent, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index dipped 1.14 per cent.
Article Summary: The BSE Sensex surged 1,502.29 points, or 1.82%, to close at 83,938.28. The Nifty 50 gained 469.60 points, (1.85%) to settle at 25,819.25. The gains followed Monday's sharp decline, when the Sensex plunged 1,483.72 points. Hindustan Unilever was the top gainer, rising 5.94%.

Article Title: Landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore as rent, filed ITR and slotted it as ‘Income from House Property’, but taxman reclassifies it as business income and raises taxable income to Rs 1.07 crore; why ITAT Sura
Article Text:
The sharp increase resulted from the change in the tax treatment of his rental earnings. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT Surat give relief to landlord?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?In one case, a landlord earned rent from and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) issued him a notice and classified the rental receipts as business income.A landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head.However, the AO reclassified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from the Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.The sharp increase resulted from the change in the tax treatment of his rental earnings. Under the “Income from House Property” head, taxpayers can claim a flat standard deduction of 30% on the net annual value after deducting eligible municipal taxes paid.When rental receipts are assessed as business income, however, taxpayers can claim eligible business expenses incurred to earn that income. This difference in the deductions available explains why the landlord’s taxable income rose from Rs 24.07 lakh to Rs 1.07 crore.The landlord calculated that if his rental earnings of around Rs 2.7 crore were assessed as income from house property, he would be entitled to claim Rs 81.52 lakh as a standard deduction under Section 24, along with Rs 1.63 lakh for municipal taxes he had paid, according to an ET report on the judgement.By treating the rent as business income, the AO denied the landlord the benefit of the deductions available under the house-property head. The CIT (Appeals) subsequently upheld the AO’s decision.The landlord then challenged the order before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Surat. On November 4, 2026, he won on the key question of how his rental income should be classified for tax purposes.The landlord’s business involves dealing in land and constructing buildings. He earned rent from industrial buildings that formed part of his stock-in-trade, or business assets. The Assessing Officer relied on this aspect while assessing the rental receipts under the head “Income from Business or Profession”.The landlord, however, maintained that his business was the “business of dealing in lands and construction of buildings”, and not the “business of letting out buildings”.ITAT Surat held that the fact that he dealt in land, constructed buildings and rented out properties held as stock-in-trade for sale did not, by itself, settle the question of how the rental receipts should be classified. The determining factor was the nature of the activity from which the income arose.The tribunal referred to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Chennai Properties and Investments Ltd. (supra), in which rental income was treated as business income because letting out properties was itself the assessee’s business.However, ITAT Surat distinguished that ruling, along with the other judgments relied upon by the CIT (Appeals), on the ground that those cases involved taxpayers whose business was letting out properties.The tribunal also noted that the Gujarat High Court’s ruling in Commissioner of Income-tax v. New India Industries Ltd. (1993) 201 ITR 208 (Guj) supported the landlord’s contention that his rental earnings were taxable under the head “Income from House Property”.The tribunal further observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that the landlord was engaged in the business of letting out properties. It also noted that no material had been placed before it to establish that he was carrying on such a business.Chartered Accountant Chintan Ghelani told ET that the landlord’s case succeeded because ITAT Surat distinguished between conducting a real-estate business and carrying on a business of letting out properties.Ghelani explained that rent earned from industrial buildings cannot automatically be classified as business income merely because those properties are held as stock-in-trade, or business assets.Under income tax law, rental earnings from letting out properties, including buildings, are ordinarily taxable as house-property income under Section 22. However, such receipts may be assessed as business income if the facts establish that letting out properties is itself the taxpayer’s business.In this case, ITAT Surat observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that he was engaged in the business of letting out properties. Nor had any material been brought before the tribunal to establish that this was the nature of his business.Ghelani also pointed out that Section 23(5) expressly recognises that a property forming part of stock-in-trade can still come within the scope of the house-property provisions. Therefore, while the classification of a property as stock-in-trade is relevant, it does not, by itself, determine the tax head under which its rental income must be assessed.In its order, ITAT Surat ruled in favour of the landlord on the classification of his rental income, holding that the Rs 2.73 crore received from industrial buildings held as stock-in-trade was taxable under the head “Income from House Property” and not “Income from Business or Profession”.The tribunal directed the Assessing Officer to recompute his income under the house-property head, allow deductions admissible under the Income Tax Act and grant consequential relief in accordance with the law.It also directed the AO to ensure that expenses were not deducted twice under different heads of income.
Article Summary: A landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) issued him a notice and classified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.

Article Title: Trump administration may raise tariffs on many countries including India and China: Report
Article Text:
Officials have repeatedly indicated that the new duties would be similar to the tariffs Trump introduced in 2025.

Why US is planning higher tariffs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Timing of announcement

The Donald Trump administration is preparing to levy higher tariffs on a host of countries including China and India, according to a report in The Wall Street Journal.The tariffs are expected to be imposed on countries that the Trump administration accuses of disadvantaging US businesses by backing their domestic industrial production, people familiar with the plans said.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to announce the findings of a months-long investigation into industrial subsidies provided by China, the European Union and 14 other countries as early as this week, according to sources quoted in the report. They cautioned, however, that the timing of the announcement could change.Greer has argued that subsidies and other forms of government support have created excess industrial capacity in the economies that have been under US scrutiny.This has enabled companies in those markets to sell large volumes of lower-priced goods worldwide, putting US manufacturers at a disadvantage.The USTR’s announcement is expected to bring higher tariffs for dozens of countries, including China, Japan, South Korea and all 27 members of the European Union.The duties are likely to apply to most goods exported by these economies, although certain industrial products, such as steel, aluminium and automobiles, may be excluded because they are already subject to tariffs imposed under a separate national-security provision.The precise rates have yet to be determined. However, administration officials have repeatedly indicated that the new duties would be similar to the tariffs Trump introduced in 2025, before the Supreme Court struck down his initial round of levies in February 2026.Countries that negotiated trade agreements with the Trump administration, including Japan and the EU, are expected to see their overall tariff rates reflect the terms of the deals they had signed before the Supreme Court ruling, people familiar with the plans said.As a result, the EU, Japan and South Korea are likely to face tariffs of 15% or less. Other countries, including Vietnam and India, could face higher rates depending on the terms of their respective agreements with Trump, the report said. The development comes even as India and the US continue to be engaged in talks to finalise a trade deal.China is expected to face steeper tariffs than many other economies, according to the people familiar with the plans.Trump administration officials have argued that Chinese subsidies are particularly widespread and cause significant disruption to the global economy.Some officials are also considering provisions that would allow tariffs on individual countries to be raised if their excess industrial capacity increases or if they fail to introduce policy changes during future negotiations with the US, some of the people quoted in the report said.The proposed duties are also likely to be imposed on top of tariffs arising from a separate measure announced in July.That action sought to penalise countries for failing to prevent trade in goods produced using forced labour and prescribed tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% for a group of 60 economies. However, the measure is facing a legal challenge in court.An announcement on the investigation this week could also shift attention away from the continuing controversy involving Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang and what the US government knew about allegations that his company’s advanced AI chips were being smuggled into China.The controversy has prompted lawmakers from both parties to question the administration’s approach towards Beijing.
Article Summary: The tariffs are expected to be imposed on countries that the Trump administration accuses of disadvantaging US businesses. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to announce the findings of a months-long investigation into industrial subsidies provided by China, the European Union and 14 other countries as early as this week.

Article Title: Trump set to hit India, China, 14 others with new tariffs after probe
Article Text:
After the set​back in the US SC over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump admins had launched two probes under Section 301.​

Section 301 probe : Govt doesn’t expect any negative impact

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union, the US Trade Representative is all set to unveil its findings in the case and propose tariffs.The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week, with Bloomberg reporting that it may come in as early as Tuesday. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe, which is likely to be followed by a set of hearings, before final tariffs are announced, in around 45 days.After the setback in the US Supreme Court over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump administration had launched two probes under Section 301.While additional tariffs of 10-12.5 per cent were imposed on imports from over 50 countries, including India, for their alleged failure to prohibit the import of goods with forced labour, which harmed American exports, the outcome of the second investigation is awaited.Going by the mood here, the government does not expect any negative impact, although it maintains that there is no structural excess capacity in India and the surplus is in anticipation of higher demand in the world’s fastest-growing major economy.In fact, during deliberations with the US government too, officials have made it clear that the government has not provided subsidy or other support to create capacity, while underlining that any country which has surplus domestic production is engaged in exports.The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. In the first probe, India had managed to get concessions with the final levy of 10 per cent imposed, against 12.5 per cent, proposed initially. The outcome of the investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework, although the final levy will be known in around 45 days. Based on the final tariff, governments will engage in negotiations for “trade deals”. India is confident of negotiating a deal where its exports enjoy “comparative advantage” over rivals from the region.While the first set of tariffs related to forced labour have been challenged in US courts, even the second one is expected to face litigation, especially because USTR findings are similar for almost all countries. In the case of structural excess capacity, among the top 20 trading partners for the US, all except Canada, the UK, Brazil and Australia are facing action, with the large European countries being part of the EU. The list also includes Norway, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, which are not among the top 20 partners for goods and services trade.
Article Summary: The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe. The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. The outcome of investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework.

Article Title: A low-Huanging fruit? Jensen burner may have netted Trump a $15 million windfall
Article Text:
Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million

TOI correspondent from Washington:
