US President Donald Trump has never been shy about claiming credit for a good deal. His latest presidential intervention, however, may have delivered a whopping personal windfall: by some estimates as much as $15 million in gains on his Nvidia stock after he persuaded the company to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.Nvidia shares surged 31.5 per cent on Monday, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value after its board reversed Huang's departure, barely 11 days after he resigned following an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese spy agencies. An analysis of Trump's latest financial disclosures by the Financial Times estimated that his Nvidia holdings could have appreciated by between $1.3 million and $15 million in Monday's rally alone.The wide range reflects the imprecise nature of the disclosures, which report transactions in dollar bands rather than exact share counts. Depending on the assumptions about purchases and sales, Trump may have held anywhere between 32,000 and 370,000 shares as of September 30. His latest disclosure, filed on November 5, records several Nvidia purchases in September, including transactions in a range reaching $250,000.Crucially, it does not cover October or November, leaving unanswered the question of whether he bought or sold shares during the period immediately preceding Huang's reinstatement.The $15 million, therefore, is a potential paper gain, not a realised profit. Nor does it establish that Trump traded on inside information. But the coincidence is remarkable enough to invite questions about the intersection of presidential influence and personal financial interests, an issue Democrats -- some of whom are also accused of being on the make -- are ready to get their teeth into.Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday. "And I convinced them ... I made the deal." The MAGA boss was not merely cheering from the sidelines either. According to reports, veep JD Vance, himself a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist, also intervened over the weekend, acting as an emissary to Nvidia's boardThe board eventually capitulated, saying it had received assurances from senior US government officials that Huang's return did not pose a national security risk. Trump himself virtually absolved Alice Huang of being an intelligence operative despite leaks from the US intel about her ties to Chinese agencies, saying any beautiful woman who comes from China is usually dubbed a spy.The White House's defence about alleged Trump profiteering is that his portfolio is managed by independent third-party financial institutions, which make investment decisions without his involvement and replicate broad market indices such as the Schwab 1000. The administration has also described his assets as being held in a trust managed by his children, although the precise management arrangements have not always been explained consistently.Experts say all this does not eliminate the underlying conflict: a president can influence the fortunes of companies in which his family-controlled financial arrangements have significant exposure. Besides, Nvidia is hardly an isolated case, although the President's broader financial portfolio makes the Nvidia episode particularly striking. Trump's latest annual disclosure, covering 2025, showed that he received more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures, including World Liberty Financial, the family-backed crypto business liked to Pakistan, and his $TRUMP meme coin. The proceeds have helped swell his conventional stock and bond portfolio to an estimated $703 million to $2.6 billion by the end of last year, according to a Reuters analysis.The growing perception among critics is that the Trump family and its business associates are making off like bandits while the President presides over decisions that can move markets and determine corporate fortunes. The concern is not necessarily that every transaction is improper, but that the administration has blurred the boundary between public authority and private enrichment to an extent rarely seen in modern American politics.The Nvidia affair is particularly striking because it follows Trump's extraordinary intervention at Intel last year. After publicly questioning the national security credentials of Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and demanding his removal over his past China connections, Trump changed course following a White House meeting. The eventual arrangement gave the US government a 10 per cent non-voting stake in the struggling chipmaker, converting $11.1 billion in government grants and commitments into shares.Trump himself described the deal as something he had personally negotiated. The government became one of Intel's largest shareholders, while Tan retained his job. Nvidia now presents an even more unusual variation of the same phenomenon. Washington does not own a stake in the company, as it does in Intel. But its influence over Nvidia's leadership, export permissions and national security standing has become unmistakable. The company has effectively discovered that its boardroom decisions can require presidential blessing.The Wall Street Journal, among others, has described Nvidia as having become, in effect, a government-backed enterprise. Huang owes his reinstatement to Trump, and the company's ability to navigate its continuing legal and regulatory troubles may depend considerably on the administration's goodwill.Meanwhile, Congress, which is itself far from being a paragon of virtue, is up in arms. Raja Krishnamoorthi, the Illinois Democrat who chairs the House Select Committee on China, called Huang's reinstatement "outrageous," arguing that neither the government nor Nvidia's board had completed its investigation into what information Chinese intelligence might have obtained. He has demanded a full public congressional hearing, insisting that the American people deserve answers.Even Republicans are asking uncomfortable questions. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, always ready with colorful observations, said it was not his business to police Huang's marital conduct while calling it “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” But a relationship with someone potentially connected to Chinese intelligence was an entirely different matter because it jeopardizes national security, he said, adding that he wanted officials to explain whether export controls had been circumvented.He also called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to answer questions under oath about the handling of the suspected chip-diversion affair.The controversy is gradually feeding into a wider Washington debate about the extraordinary monetisation of political access, a debate complicated by the fact that lawmakers from both sides have been accused of minting money with insider info. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi has faced years of scrutiny over the spectacular investment returns associated with trades made by her husband, venture capitalist Paul Pelosi.
Article Summary: Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million. Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday.

Article Title: Trump gained up to $15 million from Nvidia rally after Huang’s return: Report
Article Text:
Trump could have gained up to $15 million from Nvidia rally after Huang’s return

US President Donald Trump ’s holdings in chipmaker Nvidia may have gained as much as $15 million in value, according to his latest financial disclosures, as cited by the Financial Times.The potential gain came after Nvidia shares surged more than 30 per cent on Monday following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as its chief executive.Trump’s financial filings with the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was submitted on November 5, indicate that he may have held as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30. Based on the maximum possible holding, the sharp rise in the stock price could have increased the value of his investment by up to $15 million.However, the disclosures do not establish the exact number of shares Trump owned or account for any purchases or sales made in October and November. The filings provide holdings and transactions in broad value ranges rather than precise figures.According to the calculations based on these disclosures, Trump could have held as few as 32,000 Nvidia shares, worth approximately $5.3 million, which would translate into a gain of around $1.3 million following Monday's rally. The maximum estimate assumes that he bought the largest possible number of shares within each reported range and sold the smallest, while the minimum estimate assumes the opposite.The surge in Nvidia shares followed the company's decision to reinstate Huang, who had stepped aside following revelations about alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected by US authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence.Trump said he had been closely involved in the decision to bring Huang back to the company, claiming he had played a role in securing the outcome.“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them . I made the deal.”Nvidia's board said it had received input from “senior levels” of the US government before deciding to reinstate Huang. “Based on that input, the board is confident that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the company said.Trump also publicly backed Huang's return, writing on social media: “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”In his CNBC interview, Trump said the prospect of losing Huang's expertise to China was a greater concern than the national security questions surrounding his reported personal relationships.“The bigger threat would be losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen. That would be a threat — to me that would be a far bigger threat,” he said, responding to a question about whether Huang's relationship with a woman reported to have links to Chinese intelligence posed a national security risk.Trump also said he had discussed Huang at length with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his visit to China last week. According to Trump, Xi had spoken highly of the Nvidia chief executive.“I know how good China is … and I said to a few people, you know, I know what (Chinese) President Xi is thinking because I would be thinking like, why don’t we make a deal with Jensen?”“President Xi was saying (Huang is) the most brilliant in the world at that business,” Trump said, recalling the conversation.“Nobody understands it but a guy like Jensen, they can’t copy it. It’s uncopyable,” Trump added.“You take a look at a little wafer, and you say the complexity of that China can’t copy. Nobody can copy… most chips now are obsolete, and they become obsolete very quickly.”Huang has acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, who has been suspected by US authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence. Reports have also alleged relationships with two Nvidia employees. The Wall Street Journal report did not publicly identify the additional women or provide details of the relationships disclosed to the company's board.The board's decision to reinstate Huang followed a series of discussions and meetings, after which directors said they were satisfied with his candour and ability to lead the company. Nvidia also maintained that the input it received from senior US government officials had given it confidence that his return did not pose a national security risk.Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara on Monday, where he received a warm welcome from employees. Addressing staff, he thanked them and said he would be a “better CEO the second time around”.

The boards of Elon Musk 's SpaceX and Tesla have appointed five directors to special committees tasked with overseeing discussions on a potential merger between the two companies, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday citing people familiar with the matter.The appointments include two directors from SpaceX, Roelof Botha and Randy Glein and three from Tesla, Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung.Musk said during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that merging his AI, robotics, electric vehicle (EV) and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate umbrella would be "a good idea".He also confirmed that the two companies had formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential merger.The committees have hired financial advisers to prepare models that will help determine their negotiating positions in a potential all-stock merger, the FT reported.SpaceX has hired Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, while Tesla has appointed Evercore as its adviser, according to the report.The bankers are also assessing areas of overlap between the businesses and how a combined company could be structured.A potential merger would face significant regulatory challenges, particularly because of SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's dependence on China, the report said.Bloomberg reported earlier this month that a deal could be announced as early as December, citing progress in merger negotiations.

Article Title: Is US headed for recession? Falling household wealth, market turmoil put pressure on economy
Article Text:
US headed for recession? Report flags risks from inflation, Fed rate hikes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is the US economy heading towards a recession, or is the recent stock market selloff a temporary bout of panic? An assessment by Ionic Wealth puts the probability of a recession at 25%, while assigning a 75% chance to a market correction that eventually reverses.The report identifies simultaneous weakness in three major drivers of household financial strength - wages, equity holdings and home values - as a growing risk to consumer spending. Their decline in real terms during the current quarter could undermine one of the key pillars that has helped the US economy withstand repeated economic shocks.“Recession at 25% and a Panic That Reverses at 75%...Most of the concerns behind the selloff point to an AI build out that takes longer, rather than one that stops. A recession needs the Fed and the consumer to fail together”, the report stated.The housing market is adding to these concerns. Pending home sales dropped 17% year-on-year in October, pointing to weakening activity. Meanwhile, households have a near-record proportion of their financial assets invested in equities, increasing their exposure to market volatility.The scale of the recent correction is reflected in the performance of major US indices.The Nasdaq 100 has shed 19.8% from its October 5 peak, while the S&P 500 is down 11.6% from its October 6 record.The report also flagged the risk of monetary tightening if inflation remains stubbornly high. With inflation at 3.7%, it estimated that the Federal Reserve may have to push interest rates to 6.75% by the end of 2027 to achieve its 2% inflation target. Such a trajectory, it warned, would place considerable strain on consumers and the US Treasury.However, the assessment does not view the stock market decline as evidence of collapsing demand for artificial intelligence. Instead, it points to a possible delay in the pace of investment. Orders for AI infrastructure reportedly stretch into 2028 and 2029, while a large portion of memory capacity has already been booked.This forms the basis of the report's more optimistic outlook, which sees the current market turmoil subsiding as AI-related demand holds up and the Federal Reserve softens its policy stance after December. It assigns this outcome a 75% probability.The more pessimistic scenario, with a 25% probability, hinges on the Federal Reserve continuing to raise rates through 2027 even as household finances deteriorate. The combination could weaken consumption enough to push the economy into recession.The report identified the Fed's next policy moves as a crucial indicator, arguing that a shift in its stance before further damage to household wealth and spending could help prevent a deeper economic downturn.The next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy decision is scheduled for December 9, following its December 8-9 meeting.
Article Summary: Ionic Wealth puts the probability of a recession at 25%, while assigning a 75% chance to a market correction that eventually reverses. The report identifies simultaneous weakness in three major drivers of household financial strength - wages, equity holdings and home values. The housing market is adding to these concerns.

Article Title: Nvidia shares jump 31.5%, log biggest single-day gain since 2003 as CEO Jensen Huang returns
Article Text:
Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO 11 days after he annoucned his resignation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia shares soared 31.48% on Monday, marking their third-best day on record and their biggest one-day gain since 2003, after the company announced the immediate reinstatement of co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO and president.The stock rose as much as 36.6% during the session before paring gains to close at $165.05. The surge added $952 billion to Nvidia's market value in a single day, reported CNN.Huang's return came less than two weeks after he stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump said he had secured an agreement with Nvidia's board to bring Huang back. He also told CNBC: “I believe my intervention was very important.”Read more: Why Huang got reinstated as CEO in 11 days; crisis far from over The announcement turbocharged an already strong recovery on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51%, the S&P 500 climbed 4.73%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1,448 points, or 3.01%.Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recorded their biggest single-session gains since April 2025, when markets rallied after President Donald Trump backed down from some tariff threats.The Dow posted its biggest gain since November 4, following a sharp rally after the midterm elections.US stocks were already poised for a rebound after a punishing tech sell-off the previous week, driven by concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment boom. The news of Huang's reinstatement, which broke shortly before 9 am ET, sent AI-linked stocks sharply higher.Among the biggest gainers was AI cloud infrastructure company CoreWeave, which jumped 22.3%. Other technology stocks that had been battered in recent sessions also recovered.The rebound followed a brutal week for US markets, during which all three major indexes recorded losses of 8% or more. The S&P 500 had ended the week with seven consecutive sessions of losses, its longest losing streak since February 2020. The Nasdaq had plunged more than 5% on Friday and slipped into negative territory for the year.Markets have also been unsettled by concerns over high AI valuations, potential regulation and a possible slowdown in investment, particularly in data centres. Anthropic's blockbuster IPO last week did little to ease those concerns.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO 11 days after he annoucned his resignation. His return came less than two weeks after he stepped down following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The surge added $952 billion to Nvidia's market value in a single day.

Article Title: AirAsia trims quarterly loss, but fuel and currency pressures persist
Article Text:
File photo: An AirAsia plane takes off at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Malaysian budget carrier AirAsia reported a net loss of 381.3 million ringgit ($92.5 million) for the third quarter, as high jet fuel prices and foreign exchange losses continued to pressure its finances, even as the airline reduced its losses from the previous quarter.The loss for the three months ended September 30 was less than half the 830.5 million ringgit loss recorded in the second quarter. The loss attributable to equity holders stood at 175 million ringgit.Revenue, however, declined 8.4% to 4.66 billion ringgit from 5.09 billion ringgit in the preceding quarter, as the airline cut capacity by 12% amid efforts to rationalise its fleet. Nearly a third of its 234 aircraft, or about 31%, remained grounded at the end of September.AirAsia, Southeast Asia's largest budget carrier, has described the period as its most difficult financial stretch since the pandemic. The Iran war drove up jet fuel prices, adding to the cost pressures facing the airline.The carrier also took a 141.9 million ringgit net foreign exchange hit as local currencies weakened against the US dollar. It did not declare a dividend.The airline did not provide year-on-year comparisons, citing accounting changes following its January acquisition of the aviation business of affiliate Capital A.AirAsia said it was cautiously optimistic about the coming months, with peak-season travel and fleet modernisation expected to improve its resilience as it enters 2027. The airline is increasing capacity on high-demand domestic and international routes to tap year-end travel.But cost pressures are expected to persist. AirAsia said fourth-quarter fuel expenses would likely remain above third-quarter levels, despite a recent moderation in jet fuel prices.Its balance sheet remains under strain. Cash and bank balances stood at 905.3 million ringgit at the end of September, down from 954 million ringgit in June, while current liabilities rose to 19.2 billion ringgit from 18.4 billion ringgit.The airline, which holds about 60% of Malaysia's domestic aviation market and employs around 26,000 people, has seen its stock lose roughly 75% of its value this year.AirAsia is seeking to raise as much as $1 billion through international debt markets, alongside 700 million ringgit in local credit facilities, mainly to refinance existing borrowings.The airline gave no fresh timeline on Monday, saying it remained in active discussions with local and international financial institutions and was pursuing measures to improve liquidity.
Article Summary: Malaysian budget carrier AirAsia reported a net loss of 381.3 million ringgit ($92.5 million) for the third quarter. AirAsia has described the period as its most difficult financial stretch since the pandemic. Nearly a third of its 234 aircraft, or about 31%, remained grounded at the end of September.

Article Title: Oil prices fall as global market selloff weighs on sentiment; Gulf attacks limit losses
Article Text:
Representative image

Foreign inflows support rupee, government bonds; oil prices and US yields in focus

Oil prices declined on Monday as a selloff in global financial markets spread to commodities, with concerns over the artificial intelligence sector's ability to drive economic growth weighing on investor sentiment. However, continued attacks on Gulf shipping amid the unresolved US-Israeli war against Iran limited the decline.Brent crude futures fell 28 cents, or 0.30%, to $92.29 a barrel by 0216 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.18%, to $83.26 a barrel.Both benchmarks extended their losing streaks, with Brent declining 4% and WTI falling 5% last week.The weakness in oil prices came as Asian equity markets opened lower on Monday, following a sharp selloff in global technology stocks. South Korea's tech-heavy market dropped 4%, while markets in China, Hong Kong and Australia also traded lower. In the US, the Nasdaq plunged 10% last week amid concerns over the outlook for AI-related investments."It’s momentum carrying (oil) down," said Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at Sydney-based XAnalysts.However, Sahdev cautioned that attacks on shipping could eventually put upward pressure on crude prices."ballast (empty) vessels counts are building in crude while laden vessels are not. This risk to flows will start to price soon."The continuing conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran has kept concerns over energy supplies elevated. On Sunday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery. Multiple attacks on commercial shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz were also reported over the weekend.The Strait of Hormuz is a key global oil transit route, making any disruption to shipping in the region a potential risk to international crude supplies.Meanwhile, disagreements over fossil fuels continued at the global climate summit COP31 in Turkey. Talks collapsed on Sunday after participating nations failed to reach an agreement on including a reference to phasing out fossil fuels in the final text. It was the first such breakdown at the summit since 2009.Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing countries have maintained that fossil fuels will remain part of the global economy for the foreseeable future. Observers at the summit said these countries lobbied to keep references to fossil fuels out of the final document. The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) had also defended fossil fuel use at the summit.Meanwhile, OPEC and its allies, collectively known as OPEC+, are scheduled to hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their oil production policy for 2027. The group includes Russia and other major oil-producing nations.Strong foreign investment inflows are expected to support the Indian rupee and government bonds during the holiday-shortened week, with crude oil prices and US Treasury yields likely to remain key factors influencing domestic markets.The Indian rupee closed at 92.67 against the US dollar on Friday, strengthening past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. The currency gained 1.7% during the week.Government bonds also recorded gains, with the benchmark 10-year bond yield declining 12 basis points last week to 7.1868%. It marked the yield's third weekly decline in four weeks. Traders expect the benchmark yield to trade in the range of 7.10% to 7.25% this week. Bond prices move inversely to yields.The improvement in domestic financial markets has been supported by a shift in global investment flows away from AI-related stocks amid a deepening selloff in technology shares. India's relatively insulated equity markets have attracted foreign investment worth a record $12 billion, supporting the rupee and increasing demand for fixed-income assets.The shift has also prompted investors to unwind bearish positions on the rupee. Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian bonds in November after three consecutive months of selling, purchasing nearly $1.2 billion worth of bonds in the first three weeks of the month.Lower crude oil prices and declining US Treasury yields have further supported the domestic market, offsetting concerns over a potentially more hawkish stance by the US Federal Reserve."Indian assets have benefited from a broader rotation away from AI-related exposures, alongside lower oil prices, which helped improve the macro backdrop and supported sentiment. These will be important drivers going forward also," said Shamaila Khan, head of fixed income for emerging markets and Asia-Pacific at UBS Asset Management.A trader at a private bank said continued foreign investment inflows could support the rupee in the coming days. Market participants will also watch for signs of intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), particularly the levels at which it may step in to replenish its foreign exchange reserves.Norbert Ling, head of fixed income portfolio management for Asia-Pacific at Invesco, said Indian government bonds were benefiting from attractive carry, resilient domestic fundamentals and the possibility of inclusion in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index.However, market participants remain cautious about the outlook, with inflation, crude oil prices and central bank decisions likely to influence investor sentiment.Attention will turn to US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data due on Wednesday, followed by the RBI's monetary policy decision on December 4 and the US Federal Reserve's meeting on December 9.Markets expect both central banks to raise interest rates by 25 basis points. However, an increase in expectations of a larger rate hike by the Fed could put pressure on Indian financial assets.Ling cautioned that inflation remained above the RBI's tolerance band and that crude oil prices, despite their recent decline, remained vulnerable to renewed geopolitical tensions."The INR has stabilized and strengthened amid improving equity inflows, partly reflecting a rotation away from AI-related stocks, but the durability of this trend remains uncertain."
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 28 cents, or 0.30%, to $92.29 a barrel by 0216 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents to $83.26 a barrel. Both benchmarks extended their losing streaks, with Brent declining 4% and WTI falling 5% last week.

Article Title: Nvidia chip case: How Chinese man in Megaspeed built network serving China with Alice Huang
Article Text:
Li (left) had reportedly been working with Alice Huang for several years before the charges were filed. (Photo: X/Reuters)

How the alleged chip-smuggling network operated

Links to Alice Huang and Megaspeed

Megaspeed team linked to new venture

A Chinese national facing fraud charges in Singapore over the alleged diversion of Nvidia-powered servers to China played a key role in a network of companies that supplied advanced computing capacity to Chinese customers, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal (WSJ).The 52-year-old man, identified as Li Ming, was deeply involved in the operations and major business decisions of Singapore-based Megaspeed, and also had links to other companies trading Nvidia chips, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company where Alice Huang served as managing director. The latest report follows earlier revelations linking Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive to Nvidia founder and then CEO Jensen Huang.Singapore prosecutors charged Li and others with fraud in February 2025 over the alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. While several companies were named in the case, Megaspeed was not among them, the report said.According to prosecutors, Li bought computer servers equipped with Nvidia chips and allegedly misled the American supplier by claiming the equipment was intended for his Singapore-based company, Luxuriate Your Life.The servers were allegedly shipped to neighbouring Malaysia before being sent to an unidentified third destination. Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, where the criminal case is ongoing.Li had reportedly been working with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, for several years before the charges were filed.Chinese corporate registry records cited by the WSJ show that the couple established a cloud-computing joint venture, Century Longteng, in 2021.A social media photograph from January 2023, documenting Li's visit to a Shanghai-based AI equipment company, identified him as Century Longteng's chief strategy officer.Li, Alice Huang and Kang subsequently began building a network of partners in Southeast Asia to provide computing capacity to Chinese customers, according to people familiar with the business.They acquired the Singapore unit of a Chinese video game company and renamed it Megaspeed, with Alice Huang registered as a director.After telling Nvidia that Chinese technology giant Alibaba was an anchor customer, Megaspeed joined Nvidia's cloud partner programme in November 2023, the WSJ said, citing its earlier reporting. The partnership gave the company priority access to purchase the chipmaker's latest processors.Megaspeed brought servers to Malaysia and provided offshore computing capacity to Alibaba. However, some of those servers were allegedly sent to Shanghai-based technology company Century Litong in violation of US export controls, the newspaper reported.Century Longteng was a key shareholder in Century Litong until 2024, according to corporate registry records.Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal “no sell” list in June 2025, around the time the US and Singapore were investigating the company, the WSJ reported. Megaspeed has maintained that it “conducts legitimate and lawful business” and said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025.Singapore officials said they questioned Huang over suspicions of chip smuggling, allowed her to leave the country and barred her from re-entering.Megaspeed largely went dormant in Singapore after Huang's departure, but the team behind it is now running a new venture called Novagate Cloud, people familiar with the business told the newspaper.Established in 2025, Novagate describes itself as an Nvidia cloud partner and says it operates at least two data centres equipped with the company's advanced Blackwell chips.Shipment records reviewed by the WSJ show that Novagate received at least $300 million worth of hardware containing Nvidia chips at one of its entities in Malaysia during the first five months of 2026.The newspaper also identified corporate links between Novagate and companies associated with Century Litong.Novagate lists two Singaporeans as its director and company secretary. Both also hold the same positions at a company controlled by a director of a Singapore-based subsidiary linked to Century Litong. That director has recently been charged in Singapore with offences similar to those Li is accused of, the report said.A May report by short-selling firm Culper Research suggested Novagate was likely linked to Megaspeed, citing similarities between the companies' websites and the fact that one of Novagate's directors shared an address with Megaspeed's headquarters, it added.Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, where the criminal case is ongoing.
Article Summary: Li Ming, 52, was deeply involved in the operations and major business decisions of Singapore-based Megaspeed. He also had links to other companies trading Nvidia chips, the report said.Megaspeed largely went dormant in Singapore after Alice Huang's departure, but the team behind it is now running a new venture called Novagate Cloud.
